segments.title: The problem

segments.title: Short request, separate worker

segments.text: This pull really waits thirty two seconds. The acceptance request has already ended. During the wait, the ledger stays usable. The worker commits all records and its completion event atomically. A blocking pipe wakes one ordered event dispatcher. WebSocket then updates both tabs without polling. Moving a remote HTTP request into a worker would not bypass an upstream network timeout; this mock processing happens locally.
segments.title: The real 32-second test

segments.text: Repeating the same seed skips duplicates. Search and pagination stay in place during automatic updates. Durable events replay after a disconnection, and database transactions prevent partial batches.
segments.title: Idempotence and recovery
